data.name: Nehad
data.gender_notes: Nehad is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root n-h-d, which means to move or flow gently. This name signifies grace and elegance. The name Nehad carries the meaning “Graceful, Gentle” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Nehad usually hope their child will grow to embody graceful, gentle and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Nehad total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Nehad holds deep cultural significance in the Islamic world. It is often associated with feminine beauty, elegance, and grace, making it a popular choice for girls in the Arabic-speaking world. Nehad is also the name of some notable Muslim women of history and culture, adding to its reverence and significance within the Islamic community.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Nehad can be seen as a reminder to move gently and gracefully through life, engaging the world with elegance and poise. It is a call to be present and mindful in our actions and interactions with others, embodying the virtues of love, compassion, and harmony. Additionally, the Arabic root n-h-d is found in several verses of the Quran, indicating its deeper spiritual significance. For example, in Surah Al-Anbiya, Allah (GOD) says, "And remember the favor of Allah upon you and His covenant with which He bound you when He took your covenant, saying, 'I will place in the land h arbitrators (for resolution of the affairs) among you. Take, [therefore], that which is easily [available] and follow not that which is faulty. And know that whatever of war-booty that comes to me, it is devoted to Allah.' But the [mighty] among your men should assume no airs because of that; and they should say, 'Indeed, we have believed in Allah and in what has been revealed to us and [in what has been revealed] to Ibrahim and to those [following him] before us [i.e., all Prophets] - and we and you are Muslims [i.e., in submission to Allah]; and [furthermore] we are citizens [i.e., in Allah's land] [i.e., in Allah's protection], and we write down for those who do not assume airs [i.e., for those who show humility] and do good acts an honorable mention. And, indeed, Allah is Sublime and Compelling.'” (21:73) In this verse, Allah mentions the Arabic root n-h-d reminding us of the concept of 'ar-ruh, or gentle touch, in our dealings and interactions with others. The name Nehad, thus, serves as a constant reminder to embody this spiritual quality of grace, elegance, and compassion in our daily lives.
